I am old now, 72 years, and I have farmed this land my whole life. For my groundnuts here in Mtwara, I do what I have always done — I do not buy the fertilizer from the shop, it costs too much money and groundnuts grow well enough in our sandy soil without it. My neighbors also do not put chemical fertilizer on their nuts. I save a little manure from my chickens and goats for the plot near the house, and I plant the seeds I kept from last harvest. My grandchildren help me weed when school is closed, and sometimes I pay a young man from the village a few days to help with the heavy digging because my back is not strong like before.
